title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces
abstract: arXiv:2611.06803v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Efficient benchmarking estimates a system's full benchmark performance from a small number of task executions. Standard approaches rely solely on the binary correctness of executions from a collection of already-evaluated reference systems. An agentic system, however, produces a rich trace for each execution that can reveal substantially more about its capabilities. Leveraging this information requires useful trace representations. We propose representing a trace by extracting a structured summary of it with an LLM and embedding the summary with a standard text encoder. These representations preserve correctness- and task-related signal while minimizing the presence of system identity-, model family- and harness-related signals that dominate raw trace embeddings. translated_title: 基于缓存轨迹的任务高效智能体评估
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.06803v1 公告类型：新论文。摘要：高效基准测试方法通过少量任务执行来估计系统的完整基准测试性能。标准方法仅依赖于从一组已评估的参考系统中获取的执行结果的二元正确性。然而，智能体系统会为每次执行产生丰富的轨迹，这些轨迹能够揭示其能力的更多信息。利用这些信息需要有效的轨迹表示方法。我们提出通过用大语言模型（LLM）提取轨迹的结构化摘要，并使用标准文本编码器对摘要进行嵌入来表示轨迹。这种表示方法在保留正确性和任务相关信号的同时，最小化了在原始轨迹嵌入中占主导地位的系统身份、模型系列和评测框架相关信号。基于来自所有参考系统的每个任务执行的这种表示，我们构建系统的低维表示，并由此预测新系统的得分（摘要在此处被截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出用LLM提取智能体执行轨迹的结构化摘要并嵌入表示，在保留正确性与任务相关信号的同时滤除系统身份等干扰信号，从而利用缓存轨迹高效预测新智能体系统的基准测试得分。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes representing agent execution traces via LLM-extracted structured summaries and text-encoder embeddings, preserving correctness- and task-related signals while filtering out system-identity signals, enabling task-efficient prediction of new agents' benchmark scores from cached traces.
